title: Premium Billing Accounts — Months Counted in a Dental Tier-Difference Credit
content:
On Premium Billing Accounts, the months counted in the tier-difference credit after a dependent's Dental PPO Plans enrollment ended for loss of eligibility depend on how the account is billed; the first case that applies decides.

- **Prepaid year.** On an arrangement that carries a prepay discount (only Cascade Individual Annual Prepay, at 4 percent) and has issued a twelve-month invoice within twelve months before the credit date, only the prepaid months count: the whole calendar months from the departed dependent's termination date to the account's paid-through date, never fewer than zero, because months beyond the paid-through date are corrected when the coming year is paid. An account with no paid-through date on record is taken under the cases that follow instead.
- **In a grace period.** On an account in a grace period, only the months already begun count: the whole calendar months from the dependent's termination date to the credit date, plus one, never fewer than zero.
- **Otherwise** the months counted are the months billed after the drop: the whole calendar months from the month after the month of the dependent's termination date through the last coverage month of the invoice issued last (of two issued on the same day, the one recorded first) — that month being the invoice's coverage month advanced by its months covered less one — zero when there is no invoice or that month is not later than the termination month.

**Months covered on the credit.** The credit's months covered are the months counted under this rule less the months already credited, never fewer than zero. The months already credited are the months covered by plan-change difference credits on the dental line booked since the departed dependent's termination month; a credit counts as booked since that month when the whole calendar months from its booking date to the credit date are no more than the whole calendar months from the dependent's termination date to the credit date.

A twelve-month invoice was issued within twelve months before the credit date when the whole calendar months from its issue date to the credit date are fewer than 12. Whole calendar months are counted the way an anniversary is counted: a month is complete only when a later month reaches the same day number, and the last day of a shorter month does not complete it.

**Hypothetical cases** (dependent's termination date 31 May; credit date 20 August; invoice issued last covers July through September).
| Account | Months counted |
|---|---|
| Annual Prepay, twelve-month invoice within twelve months, paid through 31 December | 31 May to 31 December: 7 |
| Monthly account in a grace period | 31 May to 20 August is 2 complete months; plus one: 3 |
| Monthly account, active | June through September: 4 |

With one month already covered by a dental plan-change difference credit booked on 10 July, the active account's months covered would be 3.
